title: FCC Approves Amazon Acquisition of Globalstar to Advance Direct-to-Device Capabilities
summary: FCC approves Amazon acquisition of Globalstar to advance direct-to-device capabilities
detailed: In a regulatory decision issued Tuesday, Oct.
27, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) granted approval for Amazon.com Inc.’s proposed acquisition of satellite operator Globalstar.

The transaction, initially announced in April at an estimated valuation of $11.5 billion, was authorized by the commission on grounds that the combination will expand commercial competition in the direct-to-device (D2D) telecommunications sector, where SpaceX maintains an established position via Starlink Mobile.

The company will operate as an affiliate of Kuiper Systems LLC (Amazon Leo), facilitating operational alignment between Globalstar’s mobile satellite services (MSS) assets and Amazon’s low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network.
sentences: In a regulatory decision issued Tuesday, Oct.
27, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) granted approval for Amazon.com Inc.’s proposed acquisition of satellite operator Globalstar.

The transaction, initially announced in April at an estimated valuation of $11.5 billion, was authorized by the commission on grounds that the combination will expand commercial competition in the direct-to-device (D2D) telecommunications sector, where SpaceX maintains an established position via Starlink Mobile.

Industry pricing estimates published by Via Satellite place the transaction value at $10.8 billion, covering Globalstar’s operational satellite fleet, physical ground infrastructure, and licensed spectrum allocations.
Under the terms approved by the commission, Globalstar will transition into a wholly owned subsidiary of Amazon while retaining its current corporate brand identity.

The company will operate as an affiliate of Kuiper Systems LLC (Amazon Leo), facilitating operational alignment between Globalstar’s mobile satellite services (MSS) assets and Amazon’s low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network.
The regulatory clearance follows the FCC Space Bureau’s Oct.
19 grant authorizing Globalstar’s third-generation C-3 D2D satellite constellation.
